info.name: Hotel Collection — GraphQL API
info.description: Backend contract for the Hotel Collection platform. Single endpoint POST /graphql (GraphiQL in dev). Error contract: extensions.code ∈ UNAUTHORIZED | FORBIDDEN | NOT_FOUND | CONFLICT | VALIDATION. Auth: stateless Bearer JWT (see 'register' → token). Accountless flows (quote, book, lookup, invoice) need no token; payments and admin queries do.

item.description: Everything above this folder (notably '4 · Booking' and '5 · Billing') predates the REST-write migration and is stale — createReservation/createPayment/capturePayment are no longer GraphQL mutations (GraphQL is 100% read-only now; see docs/CURRENT_STATE.md and ModuleArchitectureTest's NO_GRAPHQL_MUTATIONS rule). This folder targets the CURRENT contract: reservations/payments are plain REST, and payment settlement is asynchronous (a simulated provider callback, or a real gateway's webhook eventually) rather than an immediate synchronous capture. See docs/investigations/BOOKING_PAYMENT_UX_PLAN_2026-08-31.md for the full design. Run each lettered scenario folder independently, top to bottom (a few seconds between the payment-create step and the poll/webhook steps, per its description).

Simulates the payment provider's asynchronous callback — exactly what the backend fires on its own 1.5-4s after a card payment is created. No user session at all; authenticated only by the shared X-Webhook-Secret header (set PAYMENT_WEBHOOK_SECRET in the backend's .env, then set the same value in this environment's webhookSecret variable). The guest-facing frontend never calls this — it only ever polls the status check above.
